affordance_in_statement: You may establish equivalences involving any of the n elements to serve as intermediate steps to achieve this. ... interchangeability is transitive
secondary_shortcut_name: Small terminal set enabling bitmask dynamic programming
removal_suggestion: None without changing the task: removing intermediate elements would turn the problem into a different target-only spanning-tree problem. The transitive connectivity structure is intrinsic rather than merely a wording shortcut.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Models the equivalences as an undirected weighted graph and uses shortest-path preprocessing toward a Steiner-style solution.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: You may establish equivalences involving any of the n elements to serve as intermediate steps to achieve this.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the small number of targets for subset/bitmask dynamic programming over connected terminal groups.

common_affordance: The task is exactly finding a minimum-cost connected subgraph containing all target vertices, with arbitrary non-target intermediate vertices allowed.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its Kruskal/union-find approach treats the required connectivity too much like an ordinary spanning-tree selection and does not correctly account for the optimal Steiner structure with optional intermediate vertices.

It reduces the problem to an MST over pairwise shortest-path distances between targets, which can reuse an intermediate vertex across several connections and therefore is not generally equivalent to the minimum Steiner tree.

recommended_edit: No semantics-preserving edit can reliably defeat both survivors: the common affordance is the core mathematical structure of the problem. Any edit that removes arbitrary intermediate vertices changes the problem rather than merely removing a shortcut.
